transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Hi, yeah... thanks. Um, I guess I'm here because things have just been getting really overwhelming lately. I work as an animal caretaker, and my shifts can be pretty long and physically demanding, so by the time I get home to my apartment, I'm usually totally drained. And since I live alone, it's just quiet, you know? No one else is around. 

But the main reason I made the appointment is... well, I've been having this huge problem at night. I'll go to the kitchen just to get something to eat, but once I actually start eating... it's like this completely different part of my brain just hijacks everything. It literally feels like something else takes over my body. I'll just keep eating and eating, and the crazy part is, I'm fully aware it's happening. I'll be sitting there, literally telling myself in my head, 'Stop, put the food away, you don't need this, just close the fridge,' but my hands just keep moving. I just can't stop, no matter how hard I try to reason with myself in the moment. It's just... it's exhausting, honestly, feeling that out of control in my own house, and I didn't know what else to do but come in.
After these nighttime eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or try to exercise excessively to compensate for what you’ve eaten?

Yeah... yeah, I do. It's... it's honestly the worst part of the whole night, but I just can't seem to stop myself from doing it. Like, after I finally stop eating, after I snap out of that weird trance and look around at all the empty wrappers and plates, this intense panic just washes over me. My stomach feels so stretched and tight, and my heart starts racing, and all I can think is, 'Oh my god, what did I just do? How many calories was that?' 

And I know it sounds terrible, but the panic is so loud that I just... I end up going straight to the bathroom. I lock the door, even though I live alone, which I know makes no sense, but it's like a ritual now. I turn on the faucet so I don't have to hear myself, and I make myself throw up. It's awful, it really is. My throat burns, my eyes water, and I feel so completely pathetic kneeling there on the bath mat. But in that moment, it just feels like the only possible way to undo what I just did, you know? Like if I don't get it out right then and there, all those calories are just going to settle into my body and become permanent, and I can't handle that thought. 

I don't really mess with laxatives or anything like that, because honestly, they scare me a little with how unpredictable they can be, especially since I'm on my feet all day with the animals at work. And as for exercise... I mean, I'm already so exhausted from lifting feed bags and cleaning enclosures all day that the idea of going for a run or hitting the gym after one of these episodes is just impossible. So it's just the throwing up. I hate doing it, I really do, but it feels like this desperate emergency, like I have to hit the reset button before it's too late.
During these nighttime eating episodes, do you feel like you've lost control and can't stop eating even if you wanted to?

Yeah, exactly, exactly that. It's... it's honestly the most terrifying part of the whole thing. Like I was saying earlier, it's just this total, complete loss of control. It’s not like I’m just sitting there enjoying a late-night snack and deciding to have a little more. It’s like... a switch flips in my head. I’ll go into the kitchen, maybe just intending to grab a slice of cheese or a handful of crackers because I worked a ten-hour shift and I’m genuinely hungry, but the second I take that first bite, it’s over. 

It literally feels like some other force just grabs the steering wheel. I’ll be standing there in the glow of the refrigerator light, and my hands are just moving on autopilot, grabbing whatever is there—leftovers, bread, cereal straight out of the box. And the whole time, my actual brain, the rational part of me, is screaming. I’m literally standing there, chewing, thinking to myself, 'What are you doing? Stop. Put the box down. Just close the fridge door and walk back to the bedroom.' I’m having this full-blown argument with myself in my head, telling myself how much I’m going to regret it, how sick I’m going to feel, but it doesn't matter. It’s like my body isn't listening to my brain anymore. I want to stop, I really, desperately want to stop, but I just... I can't. It's like I have to finish everything in sight before the spell breaks. It’s just so exhausting living like that, feeling like a hostage in my own body.
How often do these nighttime eating episodes happen? Are they happening at least once a week, or more frequently?

Well, it's... it's definitely been going on for a while now. I'd say, if I really think back on it, it's been at least the last four months where it's become this consistent, awful pattern. And as for how often... yeah, it's usually at least one night every single week. Sometimes more, depending on how bad the week is, but definitely at least once a week for those four months. 

I'll just be sitting there in my apartment, you know, after a long day at the clinic or the shelter, and the exhaustion just sort of settles into my bones. And because I live alone, there's no one there to distract me or ask me how my day was, so my mind just starts racing. And then, inevitably, usually on a Tuesday or a Thursday when I'm just completely drained, that one night rolls around. I'll go into the kitchen, and like I said, I end up eating way, way more than I ever intended to. It's just mounds of food, whatever I can find, and I'm totally alone while it happens. And then... then comes the panic, and I end up making myself throw up afterward. Every single time. At least once a week, for four months now. It's just become this miserable, predictable part of my routine, and I hate it so much.
Do these nighttime eating episodes cause you a lot of distress, or affect your ability to function normally during the day?

Oh, absolutely. The distress is just... it's overwhelming. It really bleeds into everything else. You'd think because it happens at night, in secret, that I could just wake up the next morning, take a shower, and leave it all behind, right? But I can't. The next day, I'm just a complete wreck. My brain feels like it's packed with cotton, and I'm just constantly obsessing over what I did the night before, or how exhausted I am, or just wanting to go home and hide. 

It's definitely starting to mess with my job, which breaks my heart because I love what I do. Like, just recently at the shelter—part of my job involves doing these community outreach events to educate people on proper animal care, and because I speak Spanish, I'm the one who leads our bilingual presentations. It's usually something I take a lot of pride in, you know? Connecting with the community, helping people understand things like vaccine schedules and spaying and neutering. But during this one presentation a couple weeks ago, I was just... I was completely out of it. 

My mind was a million miles away. I was standing up there in front of all these people, but all I could think about was just getting through it so I could leave. I was so fixated on just escaping the room and going home because I felt so gross and drained from the night before. I got so incredibly distracted just thinking about leaving afterward that I completely lost my place. I started stumbling through parts of it, mixing up my words, losing my train of thought in both languages, which I never, ever do. I was just fumbling through the informational slides, and the worst part is... I'm pretty sure my coworkers noticed. 

They were standing at the back of the room, and I kept catching them exchanging these little glances. I was just sweating, stammering through the material, and I spent the entire rest of the afternoon agonizing over whether they were going to pull me aside and ask what was wrong with me. I was terrified my supervisor was going to say something about my performance. It's just so humiliating. I care about these animals and this community so much, and to realize that this... this stupid nighttime routine is making me fail at the most important parts of my day? It just makes me feel even more pathetic. So yeah, it's definitely affecting how I function. It feels like it's slowly taking over my whole life.
